_purpose: Thirteen synthetic memory-measurement models. These are NOT validation rungs: they carry no oracle JSON, no compare.R tolerance gate, and are never fit for accuracy -- only measured for peak RSS. The 43 curated manifest rungs are too small (cbpp is 56 rows / 15 herds) to show the n*k_total memory term this set exists to expose.
_axis: The predicted allocation is 3*8*n*k_total bytes (three n-by-k_total f64 matrices in the dense GLMM workspace, src/glmm/workspace.rs): k_total is the TOTAL random-effect column count (levels*q per grouping, summed over groupings), not n alone -- 200000 rows in 5 groups is small; 10000 rows in 10000 groups is huge. before_bytes_predicted is that term for reference; it is not measured against anything, only printed alongside the observed peak_rss_kb.
_data: Data is generated at run time by gen_models.py from a fixed seed (rng seeded on the model id) -- mirrors validation/../toy28/ram_scaling.py's precedent -- and written to a git-ignored path (results/memory/data/, already covered by validation/.gitignore's blanket /validation/results/ entry). Nothing here is committed.
_family: binomial (logit) is the default family for every row unless a row says otherwise -- the allocation this set measures is family-independent, so family is not swept.

models.purpose: structured -- stresses the per-row crossed-level packing in build_packed_m
models.note: g1 (first RE term -> primary grouping under formula-order lowering) carries 600 of the 1100 total: MAX_CROSSED_LEVELS (src/consts.rs, 500) is checked only over the EXTRA groupings' summed crossed levels, not the primary -- g2+g3 = 500 stays at the dense NoZ boundary (500 is not > 500), while a primary-heavy split would have silently tripped Solver::Sparse and missed the dense per-row level scan this row exists to stress.

models.purpose: structured, widest RE in the set (headline row)
models.note: q_p held at exactly 4 (intercept + x1/x2/x3), never 5 -- a q_p=5 shape hits a known, unrelated ~2e-3 optimizer shortfall recorded elsewhere; irrelevant to a memory measurement, but avoid that shape here.

models.purpose: control: dense fallback, must not move
models.note: q_p = 9 (intercept + 8 slopes) exceeds MAX_PRIMARY_Q = 8 (src/consts.rs), so classify_design (src/fit/mod.rs) routes this to Solver::Sparse regardless of k_total -- the dense n*k_total allocation this set otherwise measures must NOT appear here. before/k_total are left null: the whole point of this row is that the predicted dense term does not apply.

models.purpose: control: LMM allocates no n x k
models.note: Gaussian with random effects routes to the LMM path (profiled REML, theta-Cholesky), which never builds the dense n x k_total z/m workspace the GLMM PIRLS path does -- the predicted term is 0 by construction, not because k_total is small.

models.purpose: control for the GLMM buffer sizing; also exercises the Glm arm of fit_on
models.note: No random effects at all (p = 10 fixed columns incl. intercept) -- routes to plain IRLS, not the mixed-model workspace. Flat by construction; this row and row 13 exist as controls for the GLMM buffer sizing this set otherwise measures, and this harness doubles as a check on the Glm/Ols arms of fit_on's build-once alloc reduction.

models.note: No random effects, Gaussian -- plain OLS via normal equations. Flat by construction; see row 12's note.
